question: Verify the entry's distinction between undeciphered Linear A/Minoan affiliation and readable Greek Linear B: sign similarity and B-based transliteration are not proof of Minoan pronunciation, meaning or divine names.
worker_disposition: partial-support -> supported (passage-level), with one entry-wording delimitation filed for reconciliation
support_scope: Three independently retrieved passages cover the affiliation/readability contrast (entry lines 11, 54-59, 66, 201). The da-ma-te leg is now documented through a peer-reviewed article's citation and weighing of Duhoux 1997 pages 291-293, not through the 1997 article itself, which remains unretrieved. Passage support is not a whole-claim promotion.

quotes.text: At present Minoan is understood to be an isolated language, that is to say not affiliated to any of the linguistic families so far known.
All these attempts at identifying the language behind the script have so far proved untenable, as not supported by enough probative evidence.
Although we are currently at an impasse at identifying the Minoan language, we understand that:

Linear A still resists decipherment for the relative paucity of extant evidence, the short and formulaic nature of most inscriptions (which therefore do not display insightful syntactical structures) and the lack of an agreed cognate language, not to mention that not a single bilingual inscription has been discovered to date.

quotes.locator: section "Script relations and 'readability' of Linear A", extraction lines 208-212
quotes.text: Linear A was used as graphic template for the development of Linear B, within a script transmission process which entailed language change from Minoan (unidentified linguistic family) to Greek (Indo-European). Graphically, the two scripts show a 70% sign similarity with respect to syllabic signs [...]

quotes.locator: section "Script relations and 'readability' of Linear A", extraction lines 220-222
quotes.text: it is assumed that most homomorphic signs (i.e. signs showing the same morphological shape in both Linear A and B) may be read with the same, or closely approximate, phonetic value in both scripts

quotes.locator: section "Script relations and 'readability' of Linear A", extraction lines 233-236
quotes.text: It is therefore possible to 'read' Linear A inscriptions in phonetic transcription with approximation (e.g. inscriptions from Haghia Triada, inspcriptions from elsewhere), although an appropriate understanding of the language behind the script still defies us.

quotes.locator: note 21, extraction lines 553-556 (attached to the sentence 'some of which have been successfully identified by scholars')
quotes.text: Yves Duhoux, 'Une analyse linguistique du lineaire A', BCILL 14.1 (1978): 65-129. Yves Duhoux, 'LA > B da-ma-te = Demeter? Sur la langue du lineaire A', Minos 29-30 (1997 [1994-1995]): 289-294. Miguel Valerio, 'Diktaian Master: a Minoan predecessor of Diktaian Zeus in Linear A?', Kadmos 46 (2007): 3-14.

passages.basis: This is the exact source the entry cites at line 11 for 'undeciphered', 'unaffiliated with any known family', 'proposed language identifications have proved untenable' and 'no bilingual or agreed cognate'. The retrieved deposit states all four in its own sentences, so the round-6 limit ('her own sentences not ground against') is closed. It also supplies the entry's line-54/59 split in the source's own words (Minoan 'unidentified linguistic family' vs Greek 'Indo-European'), and the section heading places 'readability' in scare quotes while the body grants approximate reading and denies understanding.

quotes.text: The overall conclusion, then, is clear: there is, quite simply, very little room for a random reallocation of sound values, and positive identifications of sound values in Linear A are so numerous, systematic, and based on a whole number of approaches supporting one another that, on the basis of the evidence so far, in principle the backward projection of sound values from Linear B to Linear A must be regarded as legitimate.

quotes.locator: section 3 'The relationship between Cretan and Cypriot Scripts', txt lines 293-295
quotes.text: The exact phonetic values in Linear A cannot be recovered with precision, as highlighted especially by the more complex cases outlined above, but the shared values are close enough to reconstruct the values approximately.
For if we apply the sound values of Linear B to Linear A the result is a language of which we understand neither the grammatical structure nor, with a few minor exceptions, the content.

Personal names are not a particularly good guide as there usually is no independent confirmation available that two identically or very similarly written forms render the same name [...] Linear A a-ka-ru would thus have nothing to do with Linear B a-ka-re-u.

passages.basis: The entry's line 66 caution ('applying a Linear B value to a similar Linear A sign is not proof of its exact Minoan pronunciation, much less the word's meaning') is confirmed in its 'exact' half - exact values cannot be recovered with precision and grammatical structure/content remain ununderstood - but the same chapter concludes the method is legitimate in principle as an approximation, which the entry's line 56 phrase 'useful analytical notation' understates. The name-equation examples (a-ka-re-u vs a-ka-ru; i-ja-te) independently support the entry's §9 caution that a transliterated sign group needs its documentary context before being read as a name or word.

quotes.text: Some noun morphology for Linear A has already been established. Duhoux (1997, 291-293) has argued that the prefix <i-> in sequences such as <i-da-ma-te>, which occurs on AR Zf1 and AR Zf29 means "to/in" (cf. <da-ma-te>, on KY Za2).

Another possibility is that we have here the prefix i-, meaning "to/in" (Duhoux 1997, 291-293) before a word beginning with a-, though in many cases, it is difficult to see how this could be the case.
So far, the language (or languages) of Linear A has not been convincingly linked to any other known language, though there have been several attempts at decipherment.
It does not, however, follow that the language is Indo-European - co-incidences of form can occur, and can easily be misleading.

passages.basis: The retrieved article gives the content of Duhoux 1997 pages 291-293 (the i- prefix 'to/in' argument, with da-ma-te on KY Za2 and i-da-ma-te on AR Zf1/Zf29) and simultaneously weighs it negatively ('difficult to see how this could be the case'), which is the 'contested, not a decipherment' status the entry asserts at line 106. Its independent statements on non-affiliation and on the danger of form coincidences support entry lines 54 and 59. This is second-hand for the 1997 article: the argument's content is reported by a peer-reviewed article that cites its pages, not read in Duhoux's own text.

quotes.locator: news item body, paragraph beginning 'That remains a significant if.'
quotes.text: Linear A has never been securely deciphered, and the proposed reading depends on Schumann's own phonetic and linguistic interpretations.

quotes.locator: news item body, paragraph beginning 'The proposed readings of individual signs'
quotes.text: They should therefore be treated as a hypothesis rather than an established decipherment.

passages.basis: Shows that fresh 2026 proposals do circulate divine-name readings out of Linear A (Tinu/Ida-Mate, i.e. proposed predecessors of Dionysos and Demeter), and that even the reporting of them keeps them as hypothesis. This supports the entry's line 106/201 caution that such identifications need item-level argument and are not decipherments. The preprint itself was not read, so no claim is made about its contents beyond the news report's description.

strengthens: Entry line 11's four-part characterization of Salgarella 2022 is verified verbatim in her deposited text: undeciphered; Minoan 'not affiliated to any of the linguistic families so far known'; proposed language identifications 'proved untenable'; 'not a single bilingual inscription has been discovered to date' plus 'lack of an agreed cognate language'.

Entry lines 54 and 59: the deposit itself splits 'Minoan (unidentified linguistic family)' from 'Greek (Indo-European)' and states that etymological-method affiliations (Semitic, Anatolian/Luwian, Hurrian, Etruscan) are unsupported by enough probative evidence.

Entry line 66's 'exact ... pronunciation' and 'much less the word's meaning' halves: Steele & Meissner 2017 state that exact phonetic values in Linear A cannot be recovered with precision and that applying B values yields a language whose grammatical structure and content we do not understand.

Entry line 106's 'contested etymological argument, not a decipherment' for da-ma-te = Demeter: the 1997 article's title is itself a question, and a peer-reviewed 2020 article cites its i- prefix argument while doubting it.
Entry line 201's 'any stronger assertion outruns the present evidence state': the 2026 press wave around a Zenodo preprint shows divine-name readings still circulating as hypothesis.
delimits: Entry line 56 ('conventional B-based transliterations are useful analytical notation') understates the position of the entry's own evidence base: Salgarella 2022 assumes homomorphic signs 'may be read with the same, or closely approximate, phonetic value' and that Linear A can be read 'in phonetic transcription with approximation'; Steele & Meissner 2017 conclude backward projection 'must be regarded as legitimate' in principle, while still denying exactness and understanding. The entry's caution is correct but should not read as if the literature treats B-values as mere notation.

Entry line 12's attribution is imprecise for the retrieved deposit: the da-ma-te article appears in note 21 attached to 'affixes [...] successfully identified by scholars', and the deposit's end-of-entry bibliography lists only Duhoux's Etudes minoennes I (1978); the 'unproven etymological proposal' verdict is the entry's own summary, not a Salgarella sentence about that article. The verdict itself remains defensible (title as question; Thomas 2020's doubts), so this is a citation-precision defect, not a content error.

Round-6's 'undeciphered status alone does not establish every affiliation or divine-name proposition' now has a sharper form: the literature's own position is that approximate B-based reading is legitimate while exact values, grammatical structure, content, and any divine-name reading remain unrecovered - two separate questions the entry keeps correctly apart at lines 56 vs 59.
